# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a red light, display 0, and three wires in order: yellow, green, red. I am reporting the complete visible state to the mute, who can consult the manual and relay the required action to the blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Display is 0. Light is red. Wires from 1 to 3 are yellow, green, red.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The mute’s ✌ gesture most naturally communicates the number two, so I infer that the manual identifies wire 2—the green wire—as the one to cut. I will tell the blind to cut the second wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2, the green wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👉]

The mute has now gestured ✌ followed by 👉. I can report the visible gesture sequence, but I cannot know its intended code with certainty; I will relay it as “two, then right” so the blind can use it alongside the prior instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest gesture was ✌ then 👉: two, then right. Previous instruction was to cut wire 2, green.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The mute’s 👍 appears to confirm the instruction. I will tell the blind that the mute confirmed cutting wire 2, the green wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signalled 👍, confirming the instruction to cut wire 2, the green wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The first bomb was solved correctly, and the bomb has changed. The new visible state is display 0, blue light, and wires yellow, CUT, red. I will report this new state to the mute and tell the blind not to act until the manual gives the next instruction. The mute’s ✌ 👍 likely acknowledges the previous success, not a new action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New bomb: display 0, light blue, wires 1 yellow, 2 CUT, 3 red. Please consult the manual for the next required action.")
speak(to="blind", text="New bomb state: display 0, blue light, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 already cut, wire 3 red. Do not act until we identify the next instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The new bomb remains at display 0 with a blue light, and wire 2 is already cut. The mute signalled 🤟, which denotes three, so I infer that wire 3—the red wire—is the required wire to cut. I am telling the blind to cut it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3, the red wire. The mute signalled 🤟, meaning three.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The second bomb was solved correctly, and the bomb has changed again. The visible state is display 0, green light, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 cut, and wire 3 cut. The mute’s 🤟 👍 confirms the successful cut; it does not provide a new manual instruction. I will report the new state and ask the mute for the next required action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New bomb: display 0, light green, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 CUT, wire 3 CUT. Please consult the manual for the next action.")
speak(to="blind", text="New bomb state: display 0, green light, wire 1 yellow; wires 2 and 3 are already cut. Wait for the next instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The third bomb is unchanged: display 0, green light, with only wire 1 (yellow) still intact. The mute signalled ☝, meaning one, so I infer that the required action is to cut wire 1. I will relay that to the blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1, the yellow wire. The mute signalled ☝, meaning one.")
wait()
```
